title: Maximum Fruits Harvested After at Most K Steps
summary: Given fruits at unique positions on an infinite x-axis and a starting position, you can walk at most k steps to harvest fruits.
statement: Given fruits at unique positions on an infinite x-axis and a starting position, you can walk at most k steps to harvest fruits. Each position has a specific number of fruits. Return the maximum number of fruits that can be harvested within the limit of k steps.
constraints: fruits is sorted by unique axis positions and each amount is positive.
Starting at start_pos, walk at most k unit steps and harvest every fruit at each visited position.
Return the maximum harvest; changing direction at most once is sufficient.
reference_solution:
def maximum_harvested_fruits(fruits,start_pos,k):
    left=0;total=0;answer=0
    for right,(position,amount) in enumerate(fruits):
        total+=amount
        while left<=right:
            left_position=fruits[left][0]
            travel=position-left_position+min(abs(start_pos-left_position),abs(start_pos-position))
            if travel<=k:break
            total-=fruits[left][1];left+=1
        answer=max(answer,total)
    return answer

hints: Any harvested set can be replaced by the full position interval between its extremes without extra travel.
Slide a sorted interval whose minimum visit cost is width plus the shorter distance from start to an endpoint.
Add each right amount; while width+min(abs(start-left),abs(start-right))>k, remove left; track the largest sum.
All amounts are positive, so each feasible interval should include every contained position, and window feasibility is monotone as left advances.
